Unemployment insurance provides a temporary safety net to workers who lose their jobs by replacing a portion of their salary for specific periods. Each state administers its unemployment insurance program, so the rules may vary from state to state. You must have lost your job through no fault of your own to receive unemployment insurance payments. You are not eligible for unemployment insurance benefits if you quit your job or lost it because of poor performance or another justifiable reason. To receive unemployment benefits, you must be registered with an employment agency, actively seeking work, and willing to accept work should it be offered. Your payment will be a percentage of what you made in your previous job, generally between 20 percent and 50 percent, depending on your state.
